I have been joining the class since a month ago with so many instructors and different kinds of class (i have tried them all).

If you're completely new to Pilates like I was, I'd definitely recommend coming a bit earlier, or even being the first one there if you can, especially during non-peak hours. It gives you time to settle in without feeling rushed. I'd also suggest starting with the beginner classes first. The Pilates terms and cues can be a little confusing at first, and it definitely took me a few classes to get used to them.

I'd say it's probably 50/50 for complete beginners because most classes still have people who have been doing Pilates for quite a while. But one thing I really appreciated was that whenever there were first-timers, the instructors would usually explain the reformer machine before class started and make sure everyone knew the basics.

One thing I've learnt is that every instructor has their own style. Some classes will absolutely humble you, some are more beginner-friendly, some are just the right amount of challenging, and some look so elegant but somehow still leave you sweating by the end. That's honestly what kept me coming back because every class felt different.

As someone whose first language isn't English, I also noticed that the experience can depend on how the instructor gives their cues. Some instructors are really clear and easy to follow, while a few speak quite quickly or kind of swallow their words, so sometimes I'd just look around and copy everyone else. But after a while, you naturally get used to the terminology.

The music also depends on the instructor. Some playlists are super energetic and make the class feel really fun, while others are calm and relaxing. I honestly enjoyed both depending on my mood.

I've honestly had a great experience with so many instructors, especially Shannon, Amy, Issy, Kayla, Lizzie, Denise, Jude, Peta, Yuan and Rebecca. They all have their own teaching style, which made every class feel different.

And to any guys who have been thinking about trying Pilates, just go for it. Don't feel embarrassed or think it's "not for guys." I was the only guy in the class for so many sessions, and honestly, nobody cared. Everyone was just focused on their own workout. It might feel a little intimidating at first, but don't let that stop you. Just be yourself, give it a go, and you'll probably end up enjoying it more than you expected.

Overall, it was definitely the best decision I have ever made and definitely would recommend to others! Clean bathroom, good working reformer beds that feel new. I like how consistent the class availabilities are, even on public holidays. Whilst you can make bookings to different studios on the same site, their fee structure is such that you have to first purchase a class pack for a specific studio, and you can only use the pass to book classes from that specific studio. Because my schedule requires flexibility, I tend to swap between the studios depending on both our availabilities (I wish they allowed booking at any studios instead)  however their real time updates of spots available helps. Free 2 hour street parking spots available around the area. 12 clients max per class, 50 mins per session.

Classes here specifically: as a beginner I found Max's class to be the easiest to follow simply because his instructions are very loud and clear whilst he shows you the movements, and he repeats it well so I spent less time looking around me trying to copy others because I didn't get what the instruction was (I think you'll do this anyway for any beginner, but I just found i was doing it less in his class). [{"Name":"Max Relax","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjWvB82nO5NzzXTKFxZNmkGQo5ZDH0TtxWt8TmqqSyGdnOmxSXpo=s120-c-rp-mo-br100","Rating":1,"Description":"hyde park renovation is a sorry excuse to raise the price. anything that functionally matters was not fixed if not downgraded.

there's seemingly been no maintenance of any of the machines or equipment. some bars still off deafening screeches when in use, the wooden stretch bars have seemingly gone missing, and even the leg press (edit. leg extension) was broken without any acknowledgement. (I discovered this on my first trip back post renovation. the part your feet hook under is lose making the machine bias a single leg. when using the machine with both legs as intended, it's essentially unusable and probably dangerous.)

no air-conditioning. especially upstairs is appalling. it's somehow hotter inside than it is outside on some days. not to mention, the bathrooms consistently have a foul odour from what i assume is a ventilation issue.

The club manager has since confirmed to me in writing that CCTV shows me placing my white shirt in the locker at approximately 3:40 pm, and then returning at approximately 3:54 pm and pushing the shirt further inside the locker.

However, I was then told that they could not see me separately placing my bracelet there.

I have also asked them to check the footage of me **entering the gym wearing the bracelet and leaving the gym without it**, as this may provide further evidence supporting what I have reported.

What happened to the shirt after I left it there?

This is especially concerning because Anytime Fitness North Strathfield advertises 24-Hour Security, and Anytime Fitness states in its membership agreement that club premises have CCTV security cameras recording 24 hours a day, except bathrooms.

I understand that CCTV cannot prevent every incident and that cameras do not guarantee that property will never go missing. However, when a member reports missing belongings from an area covered by CCTV  and the CCTV already confirms the member leaving one of those belongings there  I would expect the footage to be thoroughly reviewed to establish when that clearly identifiable item was moved or removed.

I was also told that the footage had initially been checked using the **fastest playback speed available**, while at the same time being told that the shirt or bracelet could potentially have been moved or taken within seconds or minutes and therefore could be difficult to identify at increased playback speed.

That explanation concerns me even more. If something can disappear within seconds and therefore be missed at high speed, then surely the relevant footage needs to be reviewed carefully at an appropriate speed.

I am not asking the gym to somehow make a tiny bracelet visible underneath a shirt. I am asking them to determine **what happened to the clearly visible white shirt that their own CCTV confirms I left there.

For a facility that operates 24/7 and advertises 24-hour security, I expected a much more reassuring and thorough response when personal belongings went missing from a camera-covered area.

I have requested that **all relevant CCTV footage be preserved and properly reviewed**, including footage of the locker/storage area and my entry and exit from the gym.

I am posting this review so other members are aware of my experience. I will also update this review if the club completes its investigation, identifies what happened to my belongings, or resolves the matter appropriately.

[{"Name":"Tito Fong","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjUdKTHYColqV4Z6pxjnGmS0o5LavDg0INMZYiJB8GE0pSb65mAM=s120-c-rp-mo-br100","Rating":5,"Description":"CrossFit 168 Alexandria (Sydney, Australia)

I stayed in Sydney for five weeks and CrossFit 168 Alexandria was the perfect place to maintain my CrossFit training while I was away from home. From the moment I walked in, it felt like a great place with the right energy, helpful staff, solid coaching, and an amazing community.

The gym itself is well set up with great equipment, and the training options are seriously varied. You can get a strong mix of weightlifting, CrossFit, and Zone/Hyrox-style training, with plenty of sessions throughout the week to fit your schedule and goals.

Most of all, the coaches are wonderful and friendly people. Whether you’re chasing performance or want to keep progressing during a trip, the community is welcoming, supportive, and encouraging in a way that makes you want to come back again and again.

And yes—these sessions are quite hardcore. You definitely have to work your butt off to finish the WODs, but that’s exactly what I was looking for. It’s challenging, well-programmed, and always feels like you’ve earned every rep.

I would definitely be back the next time I’m in Sydney. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a high-energy gym, great equipment, and a truly amazing CrossFit community.

I have been attending Clarence Street Snap Fitness and the space lacks cleanliness and is sadly filthy. Gym is meant to bring health and positive aspects to our life.

I was a previous member at Snap fitness in Perth, where the situation was very different and have moved to Sydney in the last 2 weeks. The Clarence Street location was the most convenient for me to attend.

I tried to the manager (whom is hardly ever at the reception desk and only found exercising) as to work with improvements for a filthy environment is unacceptable.

The gym has no soaps in most of the toilet sinks, stations where wipes are located is super dirty around… the other day there was not a single alcohol gel bottle filled to be used. Dust is everywhere especially weight sections. This week the stair climber equipment has a spider web right in front, with a spider hanging there.

The manager asked me to send him an e-mail yesterday, which I did. I wrote and included pictures as to the matter.  I wasn´t comfortable with the fact that I had already spoken and no one else was in copy as to address the issue. The manager replied to my e-mail on the same day, informing those actions would be taken, but on the following day I was surprised with an unexpected incident today towards me.

Today, I was surprised with a rude approach from one member, which and opted not to reply and continued with my music and exercise. I didn´t respond and wished the man “all the best” when we left the gym at the same time. Latter that day the same manager sent me an e-mail filled with lies as if I was the one with inappropriate behavior in the gym, when I was the one who received an unexpected attitude when returning the man´s towel.  The manager wrote that I had inappropriate behavior at the gym, to members and staff members. That I was no longer welcome at the gym. This is a lie and didn´t occurred at all!!

I am surprises and shocked with these two incidents which apparently might be connected… I felt so unsafe today. I was the only women and was mistreated and later received an email filled with lies. I only wanted to use one of the 3 benches, which 2 were being used and the third was occupied by his towel. I decided to wait and do another exercise. While I was doing a rep of 4x18, the man that left his towel at the beach only came once. Once I was finished, I literally went to him and ask if I could use the equipment. He said yes. Which was great. I had music on my ears and grab his towel to give it back to him. OMG! That guy, freaked out, he was so arrogant, saying he could grab the towel himself and that I was rude to touch his towel. He kept speaking rudely towards me (I felt harassed). That was just awful! I felt so mistreated by the tone of his voice and the way he kept speaking to me. I said I didn’t hear him and didn’t know it was rude to give the towel back to him. Afterward I only said: “you’re a very rude man, and I’m glad I’m not listening to you, as I have headphones on”. It was awful, really. I felt terrible and didn’t feel safe at all.

I am very surprised with this entire situation and neve had similar experience. I find this experience at this gym unacceptable.

All the best

Anyway, I was worried knee pain was going to affect my ability to complete a hike booked for April with old uni friends. I especially appreciate it when they encourage me to try and achieve a personal best or progress milestone even when I’m hesitant and overthink things. They always share my excitement and joy whenever I achieve a PB, which I’m always grateful for because it is exciting to compare myself to when I first started and didn’t know how to do any of the movements/exercises.

The group classes itself can be challenging (in a good way) but always satisfying once you’ve finished. The people who go to this gym are friendly and they cheer each other on during tough workouts or when someone achieves a PB. I’ve been a member at FORT Gym for the past three years and can confidently say it’s the best group training gym I’ve ever been part of. It’s far more motivating, engaging, and rewarding than any conventional gym I’ve trained at.

Since joining, I’ve made significant improvements in both strength and conditioning and am now the fittest I’ve ever been in my 30s. The programming consistently delivers results while keeping training fresh and challenging.

The owner Dennis, along with coaches Tom and Keely, are exceptional. They’re always available to explain movement standards, provide technical advice, and ensure members are training safely and effectively with proper form. Every class is professionally run, typically starting with a strength component before moving into a WOD that combines weightlifting and CrossFit-style movements.

One of the standout features of FORT Gym is the programming. The coaches structure training blocks with clear progression and purpose, while the constant variety in workouts means training never feels repetitive or stale. There is always something new to work towards and improve on.

The gym also offers dedicated gymnastics and weightlifting sessions each week, providing members of all experience levels with the opportunity to develop new skills under expert guidance.

What truly sets FORT Gym apart, however, is the community. The atmosphere is incredibly welcoming, supportive, and inclusive. Members of all fitness levels train together, encourage one another, and celebrate each other’s achievements. Will's eye for movement mechanics is next level. In a chaotic group class, even when you’re deep in the pain cave, he somehow spots the exact moment your form breaks down and drops the one precise cue you need to fix it. And if you do 1-on-1 PT with him, that technical focus gets dialed up even more.
